_comment: Function-length ratchet baseline, read only by scripts/lint_function_length.py (its docstring is the rule). Every function in src/maxim/**/*.py over `threshold` (200) lines is pinned in `entries` at its exact AST span (end_lineno - lineno + 1, decorators excluded) by (file, qualname). Strict equality: lower the pin when a function shrinks, remove the entry when it drops to 200 or below. A pin may only rise, or a new function over 200 be pinned, through a NEW record in `exceptions` (append-only; file, qualname, from, to, date, ref, reason, optional split_from / moved_from). `history` is the pre-v2 prose record and is not read. No writer: edit by hand with the lint's printed span. Not package data.

exceptions.reason: run_agentic_loop section 4's execute-and-learn block moved verbatim into the shared tool_dispatch.execute_and_learn (owner decision 2026-10-06), so the SUPERVISED confirmation path calls the same function; run_agentic_loop drops 3125 -> 2817 (2819 after the C5 commit). Splitting it is tracked by #1150 (dispatch, learn and after-effects steps); #1145/#1146 are fixed inside it. 379 lines at the move; 389 after the confirmed path added the human_involved parameter (+4) and the docstring its D2 and tracked-exception clauses.

Tool-failure credit Stage 2 (owner decisions TF1-TF9): both rec_outcome calls pass bridge_booked=, the signature the tool-pain bridge booked the failure under, so dispatch books it once (one keyword line each, the try and the except branch). The guarded observe it feeds was extracted from record_outcome into tool_dispatch._observe_tool_result (record_outcome 415 -> 413). Splitting execute_and_learn stays #1150's.

Tool-failure credit Stage 2, TF8 (agreed between Sessions A and C): the loop's own two rec_outcome sites pass bridge_booked=, one keyword line each (the hard rejection passes None: the tool never ran; the agent fallback's except passes the executed action's stamp, so a bridge-booked failure is not booked twice), and the agent fallback binds result = None before each action, so an execute that raised cannot leave an earlier action's stamp for the except to read. The agent fallback's routing through execute_and_learn, which would retire both sites, is #1147's.

Baseline floors B1, PR-A (docs/plans/baseline_floors_b1_build.md): the substrate_policy keyword (a SubstratePolicy that picks in place of recommend_action) is one signature line and one forwarding line to loop_substrate.substrate_tick; the selection itself lives in substrate_proposal._select_action, so nothing else in the loop grows.

The narrator sees the AUT's words: the SimulationResult.actions dict (what maxim.imagine() returns) gains one key line, "utterance": a.utterance, so a caller reading an action's words does not read respond's delivery receipt from result_output. Extracting the action serialization out of the run is the orchestrator decomposition's (roadmap 1.3.2), not this fix's.

#1260 review fold SF1: the run's own tool descriptions (LoopRun.tool_overlay, resolved once at setup by loop_state.tool_description_overlay, so a registry without tool_descriptions() fails the run before any action) reach the follow-up type as a REQUIRED keyword, overlay=, bound per run like rec_outcome: one signature line and one docstring line naming it. Reading it inside the function instead put the read after executor.execute, where a missing method booked an already-run success as a failure. Splitting execute_and_learn stays #1150's.

run_agentic_loop split verbatim into a thin wrapper (99 lines, keeping the public signature and the loop_liveness_scope decorator) and _run_agentic_loop_body (the whole former body, text identical but for its name), so bounded_stop.md's session ownership (PR 0) wraps the body in one seam (owner decision 2026-10-26, bounded_stop.md section 3 step 0). The body keeps the former pin, 2411; rule T now charges edits inside it. run_agentic_loop was retired from the 1.4.0 200-line list on 2026-10-16 (#1323), so the body is held by item 1323.functions-1000 (at most 1,000 lines, through this split_from) and by the gate's new-debt rule.
